reusable_cues.rationale: Fences a constraint against over-application by naming what it does not restrict; generalizes as scope limitation.
Sets a default disposition for an ongoing process; generalizes as a standing instruction rather than a one-off action.
Introduces a precedent from the speaker's own experience as evidence; generalizes as an appeal to prior work.

source_text: Yeah, and the thing is about, these are kind of related to stopping rules because we're not saying don't write down the terms, we're not saying don't translate the terms. We're saying when it comes to the computational process of elaborating them and filling the holes. Let's make sure we do that in a conservative way. So that we don't get an endlessly Baroque pattern language. Pfft. The honest. This reminds me of some of my work with Toki Pona. T-O-K-I-P-O-N-A.

fragments.text: these are kind of related to stopping rules
fragments.target: the nature of the proviso: a stopping rule, not a prohibition
fragments.rationale: Reclassifies the constraint. A stopping rule governs when an ongoing process halts, which is a different object from a ban or a retirement policy - and claude-1 had been reading it as a pruning policy over the library.

fragments.text: because we're not saying don't write down the terms, we're not saying don't translate the terms
fragments.target: what the proviso does NOT restrict: recording turns and translating them
fragments.rationale: Fences the constraint before it can be over-applied. Writing turns down and translating them stay unbounded; the parallel negations make the exclusion emphatic.

fragments.text: We're saying when it comes to the computational process of elaborating them and filling the holes.
fragments.target: what the proviso DOES restrict: the elaboration loop that fills holes
fragments.rationale: Locates the constraint precisely, on the recursive step where a hole is expanded into a candidate pattern which may open further holes. That is the only part of the apparatus that can run away, because each expansion creates new positions to expand.

display_cues.text: elaborating them and filling the holes

fragments.text: Let's make sure we do that in a conservative way.
fragments.target: the disposition of the elaboration loop: conservative by default
fragments.rationale: Sets the default to restraint rather than to completion. Conservative here means preferring to leave a hole open over minting a pattern to close it, which inverts the impulse the format encourages.

pattern_refs.rationale: Its conclusion is a stopping rule of exactly this shape - construction stops and hands its best family to selection when acting is worth at least as much as the best further move, or at a declared budget or stopping observation, with the receipt recording why it stopped. That is the elaboration loop's halt condition already written down.

It names the recurring choice between making new material and reusing existing material, and observes that the choice defaults toward production because production feels like progress - which is precisely the bias a conservative elaboration rule has to counteract.

fragments.text: So that we don't get an endlessly Baroque pattern language.
fragments.target: the failure being avoided: unbounded ornamental growth of the language
fragments.rationale: Names the cost in terms of the language rather than the library. Baroque is apt - not wrong, but elaborated past the point where anyone can hold it, which destroys the compression the language exists to provide.

sentences.unresolved_reason: Non-lexical exhalation ('Pfft.') registering the prospect just named; it carries attitude but no proposition, and the affect it conveys is recorded in the rationale for s4 rather than annotated here.
Dictation fragment ('The honest.') abandoned mid-phrase; the thought is not completed anywhere in the turn and no reading can be recovered from two words.

fragments.text: This reminds me of some of my work with Toki Pona.
fragments.target: a precedent from Joe's own prior work: the minimal constructed language
fragments.rationale: Brings evidence rather than an aspiration. Toki Pona holds roughly 120 words and expresses everything else by composition, which is the existence proof that a tiny vocabulary can carry a language - and its known cost, ambiguity requiring context, is the same cost a small pattern set would pay in clarifying bells.

fragments.target: the name spelled out for the transcript
fragments.rationale: Letter-by-letter spelling, the same device used for H-O-L-E, K-I-M-I and X-I-A-N-G, marking a term that dictation would otherwise garble.
